suggestions.name: Go File-Persisted Store with Mutex
suggestions.description: Creates a Go struct that manages a slice of records persisted to a JSON file, with atomic writes (write-to-temp + rename), chmod permissions, sync.RWMutex concurrency safety, and full CRUD methods.

parameters.name: entityName
parameters.description: Name of the entity being stored (e.g. Connection, Project)

parameters.name: packageName
parameters.description: Go package name

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Path expression for the JSON file (e.g. ~/.paulette/connections.json)

parameters.name: filePermissions
parameters.description: File chmod permissions (e.g. 0600, 0644)

parameters.name: idField
parameters.description: Name of the ID field on the struct

parameters.name: extraDeleteReturn
parameters.description: Optional: extra computed value to return from Delete (e.g. affected stage names). Leave empty if not needed.

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Create a Go file-persisted store for `{{entityName}}` records in the `{{packageName}}` package.

## Requirements

### Struct
```go
type {{entityName}}Store struct {
    path  string           // {{filePath}}
    mu    sync.RWMutex
    items []{{entityName}}
}

func New{{entityName}}Store(basePath string) *{{entityName}}Store
```

### CRUD Methods
- `List() []{{entityName}}` — returns a copy of all records (read lock)
- `Get(id string) (*{{entityName}}, error)` — returns a single record by `{{idField}}`
- `Create(item {{entityName}}) (*{{entityName}}, error)` — assigns a new UUID to `{{idField}}`, sets `CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt`, appends, saves
- `Update(item {{entityName}}) (*{{entityName}}, error)` — finds by `{{idField}}`, replaces, sets `UpdatedAt`, saves
- `Delete(id string) ({{#if extraDeleteReturn}}{{extraDeleteReturn}}, {{/if}}error)` — removes by `{{idField}}`{{#if extraDeleteReturn}}, returns `{{extraDeleteReturn}}` representing any references that were cleaned up{{/if}}, saves

### File Persistence (`save()` — private)
1. Marshal the in-memory slice to JSON with `json.MarshalIndent`
2. Write to a temp file in the same directory (`*.tmp`)
3. `os.Rename(tmp, path)` for atomic swap
4. `os.Chmod(path, {{filePermissions}})` after rename
5. Return any error from these steps

### Loading
On `New{{entityName}}Store`, attempt to read and unmarshal the file. If the file does not exist (`os.IsNotExist`), start with an empty slice — do not return an error.

### Concurrency
Use `sync.RWMutex`: `RLock/RUnlock` for reads (`List`, `Get`), `Lock/Unlock` for writes (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `save`).

### Error handling
- Return a descriptive `fmt.Errorf` when record is not found
- Wrap file I/O errors with context
- Panic is never acceptable; all errors are returned

Include all necessary imports (`sync`, `os`, `encoding/json`, `path/filepath`, `time`, `fmt`, `github.com/google/uuid` or `crypto/rand` for UUID generation).

suggestions.name: Go HTTP CRUD Handler Group
suggestions.description: Generates a Go handler struct with a full set of HTTP handler methods for CRUD operations on an entity, plus optional action endpoints (test, list-sub-resources). Follows chi router conventions with structured JSON responses.

parameters.name: entityName
parameters.description: Name of the entity (e.g. Connection, Project)

parameters.name: packageName
parameters.description: Go package name

parameters.name: storeName
parameters.description: Name of the injected store/repository type (e.g. *provider.ConnectionStore)

parameters.name: routePrefix
parameters.description: URL prefix for this group (e.g. /api/connections)

parameters.name: responseType
parameters.description: Response struct name if different from entity (for credential redaction, etc.). Leave same as entityName if not needed.

parameters.name: extraActions
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of extra action endpoints beyond CRUD (e.g. Test,TestNew,ListModels)

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Create a Go HTTP handler group for `{{entityName}}` in the `{{packageName}}` package, mounted at `{{routePrefix}}`.

## Handler Struct
```go
type {{entityName}}Handler struct {
    store {{storeName}}
    // add other dependencies as needed
}

func New{{entityName}}Handler(store {{storeName}}) *{{entityName}}Handler
```

## Standard CRUD Endpoints
Implement each as a method on `*{{entityName}}Handler`:

| Method | Path | Handler | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `{{routePrefix}}` | `List` | Return array; use `{{responseType}}` if credential redaction needed |
| POST | `{{routePrefix}}` | `Create` | Decode body, delegate to store, return 201 |
| GET | `{{routePrefix}}/{id}` | `Get` | Return single record or 404 |
| PUT | `{{routePrefix}}/{id}` | `Update` | Decode body, delegate to store, return 200 |
| DELETE | `{{routePrefix}}/{id}` | `Delete` | Delegate to store, return JSON result (may include affected references) |

{{#if extraActions}}
## Extra Action Endpoints
Also implement: `{{extraActions}}`
- For each action, add a method and a brief comment describing its behaviour.
{{/if}}

## Conventions
- All responses are `Content-Type: application/json`
- Errors use a helper: `jsonError(w, status, message string)` → `{"error": "message"}`
- Path params read via `chi.URLParam(r, "id")`
- Request bodies decoded with `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&input)`; return 400 on decode error
- Store `not found` errors → 404; other errors → 500
- `List` and `Get` must never return raw credentials — use `{{responseType}}` or map to a safe struct
- Include a `RegisterRoutes(r chi.Router)` method that mounts all routes on the provided router

## Error response format
```json
{"error": "human-readable message"}
```

Include all necessary imports (`net/http`, `encoding/json`, `github.com/go-chi/chi/v5`, `fmt`).

suggestions.name: Go LLM Streaming Provider Adapter
suggestions.description: Implements the Provider interface for a specific LLM API, converting its native streaming format (SSE, NDJSON, typed events) into a shared StreamEvent channel. Covers Chat, TestConnection, and ListModels.

parameters.name: providerName
parameters.description: Name of the provider (e.g. Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini)

parameters.name: packageName
parameters.description: Go package name

parameters.name: chatEndpoint
parameters.description: HTTP endpoint for chat (e.g. POST /api/chat, POST /v1/chat/completions)

parameters.name: streamingFormat
parameters.description: Streaming format: 'ndjson' | 'openai_sse' | 'anthropic_sse' | 'gemini_ndjson_array'

parameters.name: authMechanism
parameters.description: Auth mechanism: 'none' | 'bearer_header' | 'api_key_header' | 'query_param'

parameters.name: authHeaderOrParam
parameters.description: Header name or query param name for auth (e.g. Authorization, x-api-key, key)

parameters.name: modelListEndpoint
parameters.description: Endpoint to list models, or 'hardcoded' if list is static, or 'unsupported'

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Create a Go `{{providerName}}Provider` in the `{{packageName}}` package that implements the `Provider` interface.

## Provider Struct
```go
type {{providerName}}Provider struct {
    baseURL    string // default: "{{defaultBaseURL}}"
    httpClient *http.Client
    {{extraFields}}
}
```

## Interface Methods

### `Chat(ctx context.Context, req ChatRequest) (<-chan StreamEvent, error)`
1. Build the provider-specific request body from `ChatRequest` (convert `History` + `UserMessage` to the provider's message array format)
2. Set auth: **{{authMechanism}}** — {{#if authHeaderOrParam}}using `{{authHeaderOrParam}}`{{/if}}
3. POST to `{{chatEndpoint}}` with a 10-minute timeout context
4. Launch a goroutine that reads the response body and converts to `StreamEvent`:

**Streaming format: `{{streamingFormat}}`**
{{#if (eq streamingFormat 'ndjson')}}
- Read line-by-line with `bufio.Scanner`
- Unmarshal each JSON line
- Map content field → `StreamEvent{Type: "chunk", Content: ...}`
- On done sentinel → `StreamEvent{Type: "done"}`
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq streamingFormat 'openai_sse')}}
- Read SSE lines (`data: {...}` prefix)
- Skip `data: [DONE]` lines with a `done` event
- Unmarshal JSON, extract `choices[0].delta.content` → `StreamEvent{Type: "chunk"}`
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq streamingFormat 'anthropic_sse')}}
- Parse typed SSE events (`event:` line followed by `data:` line)
- `content_block_delta` event → `StreamEvent{Type: "chunk", Content: delta.text}`
- `message_stop` event → `StreamEvent{Type: "done"}`
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq streamingFormat 'gemini_ndjson_array')}}
- Read line-by-line; buffer to handle chunked JSON array entries
- Extract `candidates[0].content.parts[0].text` → `StreamEvent{Type: "chunk"}`
- Empty line or array close → `StreamEvent{Type: "done"}`
{{/if}}
5. On any HTTP or parse error, send `StreamEvent{Type: "error", Content: err.Error()}` and close the channel

### `TestConnection(ctx context.Context) error`
- Use a 30-second timeout
- Send a minimal probe to verify connectivity and auth (prefer a cheap endpoint like model list or a 1-token message)
- Return nil on 2xx, descriptive error otherwise

### `ListModels(ctx context.Context) ([]ModelInfo, error)`
{{#if (eq modelListEndpoint 'unsupported')}}
- Return `nil, ErrModelListUnsupported`
{{else if (eq modelListEndpoint 'hardcoded')}}
- Return a hardcoded `[]ModelInfo` slice of known models for this provider
{{else}}
- GET `{{modelListEndpoint}}` with auth
- Parse response → `[]ModelInfo{ID: ..., Name: ...}`
{{/if}}

## Error handling
- Never panic; all errors are returned or sent as error StreamEvents
- Wrap HTTP errors with provider name for context: `fmt.Errorf("{{providerName}}: %w", err)`
- Close the StreamEvent channel in a `defer` inside the goroutine

Include all necessary imports (`net/http`, `bufio`, `encoding/json`, `context`, `fmt`, `io`, `strings`).

suggestions.name: React Slide-over Panel with Form
suggestions.description: Creates a React slide-over (drawer) panel component with a form, save/cancel footer, loading state, and optional dynamic field rendering based on a type selector. Styled with Tailwind CSS.

parameters.name: componentName
parameters.description: Component name (e.g. ConnectionForm, ProjectStageSettings)

parameters.name: entityName
parameters.description: Human-readable entity name shown in the title (e.g. Connection, Stage Settings)

parameters.name: formFields
parameters.description: Description of the form fields and any conditional rendering logic

parameters.name: onSaveCallback
parameters.description: Description of what happens on save (e.g. calls createConnection API then closes panel)

parameters.name: hasTypeSelector
parameters.description: Whether the form has a type selector that controls which fields are shown (true/false)

parameters.name: hasInlineAction

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Create a React slide-over panel component `{{componentName}}.tsx` using TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. ## Props Interface ```typescript interface {{componentName}}Props { isOpen: boolean onClose: () => void onSaved: (result: ...) => void initialData?: ... // for edit mode; undefined means create mode } ``` ## Layout Structure The slide-over must use a fixed overlay pattern: ```
{/* Backdrop */}
{/* Panel */}
{/* Header — title + close button */} {/* Body — scrollable form */} {/* Footer — Cancel + Save buttons */}
``` When `isOpen` is false, return `null` (unmount rather than hide). ## Form Fields {{formFields}} {{#if (eq hasTypeSelector 'true')}} ## Dynamic Field Rendering When a type selector field changes, conditionally show/hide other fields based on the selected type. Use a `switch` or lookup map — do **not** use async loading; field visibility changes are instant. {{/if}} {{#if hasInlineAction}} ## Inline Action: {{hasInlineAction}} - Button inside the form body (not the footer) - Shows a spinner while pending - Displays an inline result (✓ success or ✗ error message) after completion - Does not block the Save button {{/if}} ## State Management - `formData` state initialised from `initialData` (edit) or empty defaults (create) - `isSaving` boolean for the Save button spinner - `errors` record for per-field validation messages - On save: validate required fields, call API, invoke `onSaved(result)`, then `onClose()` - On error: set error state, do not close panel ## Footer Buttons - **Cancel** (`bg-white border border-gray-300 text-gray-700`) — calls `onClose()` - **Save** (`bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700`) — disabled + spinner while `isSaving` Use standard Tailwind utility classes throughout. No external UI library dependencies.

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Create a React component `{{componentName}}.tsx` that renders a table where each row auto-saves independently.

## Rows
The table always renders these fixed rows for `{{rowEntityName}}` items:
{{rowItems}}

## Editable Fields per Row
Each row contains:
{{editableFields}}

{{#if (eq hasInheritToggle 'true')}}
## Inherit / Override Toggle
Each row has an **Inherit** toggle (checkbox or switch):
- **Inherit ON** (default): fields are read-only, showing muted values from `{{inheritedValues}}`; row has normal background
- **Inherit OFF** (override): fields become editable; row gets `bg-yellow-50` tint to signal an active override
- Toggling from Override → Inherit calls `{{saveFunction}}` with `null` to clear the override
{{/if}}

## Auto-save Behaviour
- Trigger save on `onChange` (for selects/checkboxes) or `onBlur` (for text inputs)
- Call `{{saveFunction}}` with the row's current values
- Track per-row save state: `'idle' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'error'`
- On success: transition to `'saved'`, show `"Saved ✓"` inline next to the row's fields with `text-green-600 text-sm`
- After 2 seconds, fade back to `'idle'` (use `setTimeout` + `opacity-0 transition-opacity`)
- On error: show `"Failed to save"` in `text-red-500`; do not auto-clear

## State Shape
```typescript
type RowSaveState = 'idle' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'error'
const [saveStates, setSaveStates] = useState<Record<string, RowSaveState>>({})
const [rowData, setRowData] = useState<Record<string, RowValues>>({})
```

## Table Layout (Tailwind)
- `<table class="w-full text-sm">` with `<thead>` column headers and `<tbody>` rows
- Each row: `<tr class="border-b border-gray-100">` with `<td class="py-3 px-2">`
- First column: row label with a coloured pip or icon
- Last column: save state indicator (spinner / ✓ / error text)

## Loading
Fetch initial data in `useEffect` on mount; show a simple skeleton (3 grey bars) while loading.

Use standard Tailwind utility classes. No external UI library dependencies.

suggestions.name: React Router Setup in Existing App
suggestions.description: Adds client-side routing to an existing React app that uses state-based navigation, preserving all existing views while introducing URL-based routes and query param support.

parameters.description: JSON array of route descriptors: [{path, component, description}]

parameters.name: existingNavPattern
parameters.description: Description of the current navigation pattern being replaced (e.g. useState with view enum)

parameters.name: queryParams
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of query params to parse and pass to components (e.g. tab, highlight)

parameters.name: packageManager

suggestions.promptTemplate:
Add React Router to an existing React + TypeScript app, migrating from `{{existingNavPattern}}` to URL-based routing.

## Installation
```bash
{{packageManager}} install react-router-dom
```
Also install types if needed: `{{packageManager}} install -D @types/react-router-dom`

## Routes to implement
{{routes}}

## Migration Steps

### 1. Wrap the app in a Router
In the entry point (`main.tsx` or `index.tsx`), wrap `<App />` with `<BrowserRouter>`:
```tsx
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom'
root.render(<BrowserRouter><App /></BrowserRouter>)
```

### 2. Replace state-based navigation in `App.tsx`
- Remove `{{existingNavPattern}}`
- Use `<Routes>` + `<Route>` to render the correct view component per path
- All existing view components remain unchanged — only their mounting logic changes
- Preserve all props/state that existing components received

### 3. Navigation
- Replace any `onClick` state-setters used for navigation with `useNavigate()` hooks or `<Link>` components
- Back/forward browser buttons must work (this is automatic with React Router if done correctly)

{{#if queryParams}}
### 4. Query Param Parsing
For routes that need query params (`{{queryParams}}`), use:
```typescript
import { useSearchParams } from 'react-router-dom'
const [searchParams] = useSearchParams()
const tab = searchParams.get('tab') // e.g. 'connections' | 'defaults' | null
const highlight = searchParams.get('highlight') // e.g. UUID | null
```
Pass these as props into the relevant child components.
{{/if}}

{{#if deepLinkExample}}
### 5. Deep-link support
Verify that navigating directly to `{{deepLinkExample}}` renders the correct view with the correct tab/highlight state active. This requires the Vite dev server (or production server) to serve `index.html` for all routes — add `historyApiFallback: true` to `vite.config.ts` if not already present.
{{/if}}

## Compatibility checklist
- [ ] All existing routes render identically to before
- [ ] Browser back/forward navigation works
- [ ] No TypeScript errors introduced
- [ ] No prop drilling regressions (state that was previously managed in App still works)

Return the updated `App.tsx` (or minimal diff) and any changes to `main.tsx` / `vite.config.ts`.
